meets: Tuesdays and Thursdays, with a Friday recitation

schedule.part: Part I: Foundations and unsupervised learning

schedule.topic: Overview of Machine Learning and Analytics in Organizations
schedule.note: Case: predicting drug price spikes and shortages for a 40-hospital health system

slides.caption: Data created worldwide each year keeps climbing, and most of it is never analyzed
The motivating case: a 40-hospital system buying $1.5 billion of drugs a year with a handful of buyers
Drug prices are on the rise, and a single price spike can blow a pharmacy budget
Building a price spike model from drug, substitute, category, and manufacturer features
What the shipped product claims: 93.8% accuracy on price increases, 76% early detection of shortages

schedule.topic: Data Exploration and Analysis with Python

slides.caption: Opening puzzle from a quant interview: what is a die roll worth if you can reroll twice?
Descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive: analytics climbs in value and difficulty
A short history of Python, from a hobby project in 1989 to the default language of data science
Types of variables: numeric, categorical, ordinal, binary, and dates
Group by and aggregate: the pandas move behind most business questions

schedule.topic: Recitation: Data Sourcing, Cleaning, and Visualization

slides.caption: Flat files: the same data as CSV, JSON, and Excel
How an API works: your code asks a server, the server answers with data
Market data APIs like Alpha Vantage put live prices one request away
Data professionals spend as much as 80% of their time cleaning and organizing data
The Python visualization libraries, from Matplotlib to Plotly

schedule.note: Clustering project kicks off: segmenting credit card customers

slides.caption: Plain, spicy, extra chunky: Howard Moskowitz found segments where others saw one market
Clustering for policy: finding eligible households that never enroll in SNAP or Medicaid
K-means in four steps: place centroids, assign points, recompute, repeat
The elbow method: add clusters until the error stops falling fast
Same rings, two algorithms: k-means cuts them into wedges, DBSCAN follows the shape
The Hughes phenomenon: past some point, more features make a classifier worse
Seventeen foods across four UK nations. Which country is the odd one out?
A principal component is a direction in the 17-dimensional space of food types
Squeezing square footage and number of rooms onto one line of best fit
Feature engineering: imputation, outliers, one-hot encoding, log transforms, scaling
Inference versus prediction: explaining the world or forecasting it
A policy regression: do workforce training programs raise earnings after six months?
The assumptions of linear regression, and what breaks when each one fails
A decision tree splits movies into hits and flops on stars and budget
From one tree to many: bagging builds random forests, boosting builds gradient boosted trees

schedule.topic: Classification Theory and Methods, with a guest lecture on machine learning for product data science
schedule.note: Guest lecture from a CMU alum working as a product data scientist; lab on telco customer churn

slides.caption: Amazon's resume screener learned to penalize the word women's. What went wrong?
Generalization: training error keeps falling while test error turns back up
The ROC curve: every threshold traded off between catching positives and false alarms
LIME on a wolf-versus-husky classifier: the model was looking at the snow
SHAP values: how much each feature pushed a mushroom toward poisonous
U.S. retail sales: a steady trend with a holiday spike every year
Random noise, trends, and seasonality: the patterns a forecast has to separate
Duolingo daily active users, 2020 to 2024
Google's stock price after differencing: the trend is gone, the noise remains
Prophet decomposes a series into trend, seasonality, and holidays

schedule.part: Part III: Experiments, language, and vision

schedule.note: No class Tuesday. Case: game design at Cookie Cats. Midterm projects due March 15

slides.caption: An A/B test: split the audience, show each half a version, compare conversion
How sad should Duo be? Even a mascot's expression is something you can test
Dropping capitalization looked harmless and cost 0.5% of day-one retention
Cookie Cats moved the first gate from level 40 to level 30. Did players stay longer?
Bandits: an A/B test that shifts traffic to the winner while it is still running

schedule.topic: Natural Language Processing Theory and Methods

slides.caption: Structured versus unstructured data, and why most of an organization's data is text
English is 59% of web content but is spoken by about 20% of the world
Stemming versus lemmatization: two ways to reduce words to their roots
Word embeddings place words with similar meanings near each other
Classical NLP pipelines gave way to deep learning in about five years
From a biological neuron to an artificial one: weighted inputs and an activation
A handwritten digit is 784 pixels, each an activation between 0 and 1
The hope for hidden layers: digits built from loops and strokes
A single neuron can learn OR and AND, but not every pattern
Forward propagation makes a prediction, backpropagation assigns the blame
Pretraining is like compressing a chunk of the internet into a file of weights
At bottom, a language model predicts the next word
How to train a chatbot: pretrain a base model, then fine-tune it into an assistant
Scaling laws: loss falls predictably with more parameters and more data
In one clinical study, the LLM alone beat doctors using conventional resources on diagnostic reasoning

schedule.topic: Text Mining with Large Language Models
schedule.note: Lab week, short for Spring Carnival. Language model project due: routing student loan complaints

slides.caption: CheXNet: detecting pneumonia from chest X-rays at the level of radiologists
Object detection: boxing every car and person on a busy street
Add a little noise and a panda becomes a gibbon at 99% confidence
ImageNet error rates fell below the 5.1% human benchmark
A vertical edge detection kernel, the basic move inside a convolutional network

schedule.topic: Case: Tesla Vision vs. Waymo Sensor Fusion, and course wrap-up
schedule.note: Computer vision project due. Final projects due April 30

slides.caption: The six levels of driving automation, from none to full
Waymo: 29 cameras, 5 lidar, 6 radar. Tesla: 9 cameras and vision alone
How a self-driving car sees: cameras, short and long range radar, and lidar
The toolkit built over the semester, from k-means to transformers

assignments.name: In-class exercises and participation
assignments.description: Lecture days end with a short two or three question quiz on Canvas. Lab days end with submitting the code we wrote together, graded pass/fail.

assignments.name: Quizzes
assignments.description: Weekly open-book quizzes on Canvas covering lectures and readings, about 15 to 20 minutes each, with the two lowest scores dropped. No generative AI on quizzes.

assignments.name: Mini-labs
assignments.description: Short individual labs of one to two hours, graded on completion, each starting from a notebook. Topics include avocado prices and sales across U.S. markets, feature engineering and PCA on a 70-column real estate dataset, random forests predicting home sale prices, predicting which households drop out of a subsidized broadband program, and NLP on CFPB student loan complaints.

assignments.name: Applied ML projects
assignments.description: Four projects in groups of up to three, graded the way a professional deliverable would be. Clustering segments credit card customers with k-means and at least two methods for choosing the number of clusters. Classification models customer retention at a student travel company. The language model project has a model reclassify student loan complaints into six policy categories, check agreement between models with Cohen's kappa, and test whether models can score complaint severity. The last project applies computer vision.

assignments.name: Midterm project
assignments.description: Groups pick a decision problem for a public agency, nonprofit, or mission-driven organization and answer it with clustering, regression, or classification. Deliverables are an 8 to 12 page paper and a short presentation at the start of a class in the second half of the term.

assignments.name: Final project
assignments.description: A policy question of the group's own, or one I define (legislative text, public comment sentiment, satellite imagery), answered with NLP, neural networks, language models, or vision. Deliverables are a one-page proposal, a 5 to 10 page report, and a 3 to 5 minute pitch on the last day of class.
